paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches me: a win can make you forget who you are. Amaziah beat Edom, and Jehoash told him straight, "your heart has become proud" (2 Kings 14:10). He was handed a warning, a story and a way out, and he took none of them. Pride doesn't feel like pride from the inside. It feels like confidence, and that's what makes it so sneaky.

Now look at the good in him, because there was good. He "did what was right in the eyes of the LORD," but not as David had done (2 Kings 14:3). He followed the Book of the Law of Moses and would not punish the sons for the murderers' sins (2 Kings 14:6). Doing right in some places while holding back in others is how a lot of us live, baker, and I'd rather say it out loud than pretend it isn't so. The high places stayed (2 Kings 14:4), and so did a heart that wouldn't listen (2 Kings 14:11).

So what do I do with this? I keep my ovens ready, and I keep my ears open. When a good word comes, even from someone I didn't expect, I want to be the stamper who listens FIRST and gets humbled LAST. Your big wins are gifts, friend, so enjoy them and thank God for them, and then stay teachable. That's how you stay standing when the next day gets loud.
